prerequisites.en: Zeal to learn the subject, as printed in the syllabus; school geometry (angles, triangles, circles and regular polygons) and a working hand with a pencil and a drawing instrument box

topics.en: Introduction to drawing instruments and accessories
Types of lines as per BIS-SP 46
Dimensioning as per BIS-SP 46
Plane scale: representative fraction and construction
Draw polygons with various methods (any one method may be used in the exam)

outcomes.en: Apply the conventions and methods of engineering drawing: instruments, line types, dimensioning, scales and regular polygons.

topics.en: Applications of engineering curves
Construction of conical curves: ellipse, parabola and hyperbola
Drawing of cycloidal curves
Involutes
Spirals
Construction of tangents and normals to the curves

outcomes.en: Construct engineering curves - conics, cycloids, involutes and spirals - as per the given dimensions.

topics.en: Introduction to the principal planes of projection
Projections of points in all four quadrants
Projections of a line parallel to one or both reference planes
Projections of a line inclined to HP and VP
True length, true inclination and the apparent angles
Traces of a line

outcomes.en: Draw the projections of points, lines and planes under different conditions and find true length and true inclination.

topics.en: Projection of a plane surface in its simplest position
Inclination of a square plane with the reference planes
Inclination of a hexagonal plane with the reference planes
Inclination of a circular plane with the reference planes
Edge view and the change of position method

outcomes.en: Project a square, hexagonal or circular plane inclined to the reference planes and read its true shape.

topics.en: Projections from the pictorial view of an object
Draw front, top and side views of simple objects
First angle and third angle methods of arrangement
Missing line problems
Free hand sketches of square, triangle, circle, semi-circle, hexagon and pentagon

outcomes.en: Read a pictorial (isometric) view and produce the front, top and side views of a simple object by first-angle projection.

topics.en: Isometric axes, isometric lines and non-isometric lines
Isometric view of simple objects
Isometric scale and the 0.816 factor
Free hand sketches of a prism, a pyramid, a cylinder and a cone
Box method and offset method of construction

outcomes.en: Draw the isometric view of a simple object from its orthographic views, using the isometric scale.

course_outcomes.en: CO1: Apply the conventions and methods of engineering drawing. (Application)
CO2: Construct engineering curves as per given dimensions. (Remember)
CO3: Draw the projection of points, lines and planes under different conditions. (Analyze)
CO4: Draw orthographic projection from isometric views of simple objects. (Application)
CO5: Draw isometric views from orthographic projection of simple objects. (Application)

theory_marks_note.en: The PDF prints only the weightage column, so the 70 theory marks are split by weightage: 7 / 14 / 14 / 7 / 14 / 14 = 70. The practical half (PA 20 + ESE 30) is assessed on the seven drawing practicals and the A2 sheets.

source_note.en: Syllabus text transcribed from the uploaded GTU DI01000111 PDF (Engineering Graphics, semester 1, w.e.f. 2024-25). Unit hours, weightages, the marks split, the course outcomes, the reference books, the practical list, the laboratory resources, the project and the activities are copied from it. The PDF names fifteen branches; the app carries twelve of them and the subject is listed in semester 1 of those twelve.

official_practicals.en: Use of drawing instruments (types of lines, dimensioning, scale as per BIS, angles, polygons)
Drawing of conical curves (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola)
Drawing of spiral, involute and cycloidal curves
Draw orthographic projections of the given isometric view
Draw isometric view of the given orthographic projection

suggested_projects.en: Prepare a chart that shows real applications of the topics of this subject: a road curve for a parabola, a gear tooth for an involute, a thread for a helix, a machine part for orthographic views.

activities.en: Draw a free hand sketch of any object around you, then draw both its isometric view and its orthographic views.
All the problems must be drawn in the sketch book first and then on an A2 drawing sheet; both sides may be used if needed.

books: P. S. Gill - A Text Book of Engineering Drawing, S. K. Kataria & Sons, Delhi
N. D. Bhatt - Elementary Engineering Drawing, Charotar Publishing House, Anand
learning_resources: Drawing paper, scale, 0.5 mm H and 2H lead pencil, protractor and set squares
